text: Domain 3 covers what happens after a solution is built and running — the Monitoring Hub, Direct Lake Mode's fallback behavior, capacity sizing, and scoped-down production practices from Course 3.

Direct Lake Mode lets a semantic model read Delta files straight from OneLake without importing. The exam-tested detail is the fallback: a too-large table silently reverts to DirectQuery instead of failing outright.
The Monitoring Hub shows run history and duration for every pipeline, notebook, and Dataflow in a workspace — it's where you'd actually go to diagnose that kind of slowdown.
Capacity throttling shows up as jobs queuing during peak hours — check capacity utilization first. Root-cause questions ask for the single correct next diagnostic step, not a full playbook.
Direct Lake's fallback to DirectQuery is the single highest-yield performance fact in this domain. Next up: practice questions on OneLake and Lakehouses.
